headline: The Model Cleaned Up After The Games Were Already Over
paragraphs: Fair warning before anyone frames the number: Week 3 was graded in hindsight, which means the model got to fill out its card with the box scores sitting right there. It went 40-25-1 on 66 plays for +110.47 and a 16.7 percent ROI. Impressive in the way that shooting free throws in an empty gym is impressive. The real ledger still reads zero weeks graded, zero plays, zero dollars.

Inside the retrospective fantasy, the spread was doing the heavy lifting: 26-13-1 across 40 plays, +106.34, a 26.6 percent ROI. Totals went 8-8 for a loss of 7.28, which is a lot of typing for nothing, and the ten moneylines came back 6-4 and +11.41. Best call was Northern Illinois plus 34.5 at a 9.6 point edge, cashed by a mile in a 42-17 game. The model's favorite loser was Florida International at plus 225, a 12.4 point edge that finished 16-10 the wrong way.

The part that actually happened in public is the part that hurt. The published top five went 2-3 for minus 11.82 and a negative 23.6 percent ROI, off an expected win rate of 68.1 percent. So the model hit 61.5 percent on the 66 games nobody was watching and 40 percent on the five it stood behind. Overall win rate matched the expectation exactly, which is either calibration or the universe's driest joke.
